description: PEA organizes assistance governance around three design questions: what forms of assistance are allowed or restricted (Policy), how those boundaries are implemented (Enforcement), and who can control them during use (Authority).
title: PEA (Policy, Enforcement, and Authority) analytic lens

description: The article operationalizes sociocultural design variation with a coding scheme crossing the pentad facets: Participants (P0 teacher, P1 non-authentic practitioners, P2 authentic practitioners), Setting (S0 classroom, S1 non-authentic settings, S2 authentic settings), Time (T0 educational timeframe,
title: Pentad-based coding scheme (P, S, T, CS, CL) for classifying authentic CSCL designs

description: The linking step maps each independently calibrated period to a common reference metric by minimizing a response-count-weighted pseudo-Huber (robust Haebara) discrepancy between expected-score curves on anchor items.
title: Per-draw robust linking

description: PND is a non-parametric measure for evaluating single-subject research, calculated by dividing the number of treatment-phase data points exceeding the highest baseline data point by the total treatment data points and multiplying by 100.
title: Percentage of non-overlapping data (PND) with Scruggs and Mastropieri effectiveness cutoffs

description: The article frames person-centered analysis as a methodological framework that identifies subgroups of individuals based on how variables interrelate within people, in contrast to variable-centered analysis's \"one-size-fits-all\" aggregate estimates.
title: Person-centered (cluster) analysis

description: The article proposes testing a theory's relative universalism—functional forms invariant while parameter magnitudes vary—by combining latent profile analysis with within-profile structural equation modeling.
title: Person-centered latent-profile analysis for testing relative universalism of psychological theories

description: The article advances a framework in which interventions that alter physiological or motivational states in predictable ways serve as diagnostic tools for probing the organization of cognitive systems, analogous to lesion studies and pharmacological or stimulation manipulations.
title: Perturbation-based framework: structured interventions as diagnostic probes of cognitive architecture
